angle: Terezín (Theresienstadt) population, crowding, deaths, deportations, and children's survival statistics (1941-1945)
prompt: Research verified demographic and mortality statistics for the Theresienstadt (Terezín) ghetto-camp from November 1941 to May 1945, using USHMM (United States Holocaust Memorial Museum), Yad Vashem, Památník Terezín (Terezín Memorial), Terezín Initiative (Institut Terezínské iniciativy), and H.G. Adler. Gather exact figures with units, years, and source citations (with URLs) for: (1) pre-war civilian/garrison population of Terezín and total town footprint/area vs. peak ghetto population (September 1942) and average living space per prisoner; (2) total number of Jewish prisoners sent to Terezín (1941-1945) broken down by country/origin where available; (3) deaths inside Terezín itself (total and peak monthly mortality, primary causes like starvation/typhus/dysentery); (4) total deported east from Terezín (to Auschwitz-Birkenau, Treblinka, Maly Trostinets, Sobibor, etc.) and how many deportees survived; (5) number of prisoners liberated at Terezín in May 1945; (6) specifically, how many children (under age 15) were imprisoned in Terezín and how many survived—explicitly documenting the popular '15,000 children / ~100 survived' vs. exact modern Terezín Initiative / Památník Terezín archival counts and why scholarly counts differ (e.g., age cutoffs <14 vs <15 vs <18, children born in Terezín, children who survived in Terezín vs. after transport).

angle: The June 23, 1944 ICRC (Red Cross) inspection, Stadtverschönerung, and the 1944 propaganda film
prompt: Research verified historical facts on the Nazi 'beautification' (Stadtverschönerung) of Terezín, the June 23, 1944 International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) delegation visit, and the 1944 propaganda film, using USHMM, Yad Vashem, Památník Terezín, ICRC archives/scholarship, and Jewish Museum in Prague. Gather exact figures, dates, names, and sources (with URLs) for: (1) deportations carried out immediately BEFORE the June 23, 1944 visit to reduce visible overcrowding (May 1944 transports to Auschwitz-Birkenau, exact dates and headcount); (2) specific staged props and changes made during Stadtverschönerung (fresh paint, fake shops/café/bank, children's pavilion, Hans Krása's opera Brundibár, reduced barracks density along the tour route, street signs); (3) who attended the June 23, 1944 inspection (Swiss ICRC delegate Dr. Maurice Rossel, Danish officials Eigil Juel Henningsen and Frants Hvass), exact duration of the visit in hours, the pre-planned route, what Rossel was prevented from seeing or failed to inspect, and what Rossel's official report and photographs concluded; (4) the 1944 propaganda film directed under coercion by Kurt Gerron ('Theresienstadt. Ein Dokumentarfilm aus dem jüdischen Siedlungsgebiet' — also check and myth-check the popular unofficial title 'Der Führer schenkt den Juden eine Stadt'): exact filming dates (August-September 1944), and the autumn 1944 liquidating transports (September-October 1944, exact count deported including Gerron, Brundibár cast/children, and Council of Elders).

angle: I Never Saw Another Butterfly, Friedl Dicker-Brandeis, and Pavel Friedmann ('The Butterfly', 4. 6. 1942)
prompt: Research verified archival facts about 'I Never Saw Another Butterfly', Friedl Dicker-Brandeis, and Pavel Friedmann using the Jewish Museum in Prague, USHMM, Yad Vashem, Památník Terezín, and US/Czech copyright/publication records. Gather exact figures, dates, and sources (with URLs) for: (1) Friedl Dicker-Brandeis's clandestine art classes in Terezín (how many children she taught, how many drawings she packed into two suitcases before her October 6, 1944 transport to Auschwitz, where she was murdered Oct 9, 1944); (2) exact count of surviving children's drawings and poems held by the Jewish Museum in Prague (often cited ~4,000 or ~4,387 drawings, ~66+ poems—verify exact archive figures and why counts vary); (3) publication history of the anthology (Hana Volavková editor, 1959 Czech first edition, 1962/1964 English editions by McGraw-Hill / Schocken, who translated 'The Butterfly'—check Ewald Osers vs. Jeanne Němcová vs. Edith Pargeter); (4) Pavel Friedmann's verified biography: birth date/place (Jan 7, 1921, Prague—note he was 21 when he wrote 'The Butterfly' on June 4, 1942, NOT a young child! Verify this carefully!), date deported to Terezín (Apr 26, 1942 — check 'seven weeks' line!), date deported to Auschwitz (Sept 29, 1944), and date/place of death; (5) exact Czech and English copyright/public-domain status of Pavel Friedmann's 1942 poem and the English translation in 'I Never Saw Another Butterfly'.

angle: Vedem magazine, Home L417 (Boys' Home I), contributors, survival counts, and Pepek's editorial
prompt: Research verified historical facts about the clandestine boys' magazine 'Vedem' in Home I of Building L417 at Terezín, using vedem-terezin.cz, Památník Terezín, USHMM, Yad Vashem, and the Jewish Museum in Prague / Terezín Initiative. Gather exact figures, dates, and sources (with URLs) for: (1) when Vedem was founded and ended (Dec 18, 1942 to summer/July 1944), how often it was produced (weekly Friday readings), and total surviving pages (~800 pages across how many surviving issues?); (2) Home I / L417 structure: what L417 was (former boys' school), how many boys lived in Room 1 ('Republic of Škid') vs. L417 overall, ages (approx. 12-15), and head educator Valtr Eisinger; (3) key creators and their fates: Petr Ginz (founder/editor 'nz', exact dates, Moon Landscape, deportation/murder), Jiří Kurt Kotouč, Hanuš Hachenburg, Zdeněk Taussig (how he hid the Vedem pages in the blacksmith's forge/smithy until liberation); (4) specifically Josef 'Pepek' Stiassny—author of the 'Loonie / idiot' editorial at https://www.vedem-terezin.cz/en/rambles/22.html: verify his full name, birth date, arrival in Terezín, transport to Auschwitz, survival or death, and exact date/issue number of that editorial + translator/license terms on vedem-terezin.cz; (5) how many boys of Room 1 / Home L417 / Vedem contributors survived the Holocaust (check exact figures vs. 'out of ~100 boys in Room 1, ~15 survived' or similar claims, preserving source disagreements).

angle: License-verified historical photographs of Terezín, 1944 Red Cross / film stills, Vedem pages, and Terezín art/memorials
